hypothesis: Reusing one verified Hyperliquid REST completed-minute candle snapshot per non-profit-lock symbol, while preserving every transport observation for completed-bar profit-lock symbols, can reduce V58 shared-IP request weight without changing entry routing or exit-controller decisions.
decision: Revise rather than promote the cache challenger. The prior all-eight-symbol cache is not eligible for live use because V58 recomputes an unrecorded completed-bar profit lock on every poll and Hyperliquid's official candleSnapshot documentation does not guarantee that the first returned completed candle is immutable. Automatically bypass caching for every symbol derived from configured profit-lock history requirements; V58 currently derives only xyz:SP500. Retain the existing live runner unchanged and uncached. Continue the preregistered 1,440-minute parity watcher, then validate exact routing on identical input windows before any approval request.
falsifier: Reject the selective cache challenger if any configured completed-bar profit-lock symbol is cached; if a synthetic late candle revision is not visible to the profit-lock controller on its next poll; if any internal missing row, conflicting duplicate, or cached-versus-uncached OHLCV mismatch appears for cacheable symbols; if identical completed-bar inputs change entry or exit decisions; or if measured shared-IP pressure and degraded cycles do not improve after an authority-none prospective run.
limitations: The prior 70 percent request-reduction threshold is not met by the safer selective design; the ideal call reduction is 65.625 percent before endpoint response-weight and retry effects.
Hyperliquid documents candleSnapshot fields, the 5,000-candle limit, rate-limit weights, and WebSocket candle subscriptions, but does not document first-completed-response immutability.
Live market-candle telemetry publishes only unseen timestamps, so the current DuckDB parity report cannot reveal a correction to an already published timestamp.
The synthetic correction proves a possible semantic difference; it does not establish that Hyperliquid has revised a completed V58 candle in production.
The active observer process was not restarted, so the durable 1,440-minute prefix continues under its originally loaded all-symbol cache implementation.
Exact OHLCV equality does not yet prove route, entry-freshness, opposite-exit, maximum-hold, or completed-bar profit-lock decision parity.
No profitability conclusion follows from transport reliability evidence.
